## Context / Problem

`import rebar` callers get a return value, not a terminal, so the first-class way to raise
a non-fatal warning is Python's dedicated **`warnings`** subsystem (not `logging`, which is
silent unless the app configures it, and which the brainstorm explicitly rejected as "log
only"). This story emits a `warnings.warn` of a dedicated category from single-ticket
library functions when the detector fires.

Depends on the detector (`cross_session_warning_for`, sibling story — merged) and the
reducer clearing (merged). A ticket that is not `in_progress` has no holder, so the detector
returns `None` and no warning is emitted.

## Approach

Define a dedicated warning category `class CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)` and a single
best-effort emit helper in a small new module `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py`, and re-export the
category from the package (`rebar.CrossSessionWarning`) so callers can filter/escalate it
precisely with the stdlib `warnings` filters.

The helper mirrors the CLI's `_maybe_warn_cross_session`
(`src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py:60`) — it is **best-effort and must never break the call**:

```python
# src/rebar/_lib_warn.py
import warnings

class CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning):
    """Raised (via warnings.warn) when a single-ticket rebar library call targets a
    ticket whose live in_progress claim is held by a different session."""

def emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, *, repo_root=None, stacklevel: int = 3) -> None:
    """Best-effort: warn when another session holds ticket_id; never raise.

    Any detector error (corrupt/absent/locked state) is swallowed so the underlying
    library operation always proceeds. stacklevel defaults to 3 so the warning is
    attributed to the *caller of the public library function* (user -> public fn ->
    this helper -> warnings.warn), not to rebar-internal frames.
    """
    try:
        from rebar._commands.cross_session import cross_session_warning_for

        msg = cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)
        if msg is not None:
            warnings.warn(msg, CrossSessionWarning, stacklevel=stacklevel)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — advisory warning must never break the call
        pass
```

Each single-ticket public library entry point calls
`emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` **before** returning (and,
for writes, before performing the mutation, so the warning is computed against the
pre-mutation holder — matching the CLI/MCP surfaces). When the detector returns `None`
nothing is emitted. **No function's return type changes** — the warning rides the
`warnings` channel, matching the "all surfaces first-class without a return-shape change"
decision.

The single-ticket public functions to cover, at their **actual definition sites** (verified
against the current tree; the public names are the ones re-exported from
`src/rebar/__init__.py`):

- Reads — `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py`: `show_ticket` (`:40`), `deps` (`:172`).
- Writes — `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`: `transition` (`:272`), `reopen` (`:455`).
- Mutations — `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`: `comment` (`:55`), `edit_ticket` (`:147`)
  (the public name is **`edit_ticket`**, not `edit`; re-exported as `rebar.edit_ticket`),
  `link` (`:181`), `unlink` (`:205`), `tag` (`:221`), `untag` (`:234`), `archive` (`:247`).
- Gates — `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py`: `set_file_impact` (`:129`),
  `declare_no_file_impact` (`:141`).

**`link` / `unlink` take two endpoints** (`id1, id2, relation`). The warning is computed for
the **primary endpoint `id1`** only (the first positional ticket argument), matching the
CLI (S3) and MCP (S4) surfaces — pass `id1` to `emit_cross_session_warning`.

Bulk reads (`list_tickets`, `search`, `ready`, `next_batch`) do **not** warn. `claim` is
excluded: claiming an already-`in_progress` ticket raises `ConcurrencyError` before any
warning path (`docs/concurrency.md`).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py` (**new**) — define `CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)` and the
  best-effort `emit_cross_session_warning` helper (try/except-contained detector call +
  `warnings.warn`).
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — re-export `CrossSessionWarning` (import + `__all__`).
- `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py` — call the helper in `show_ticket` and `deps`.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — call the helper in `transition` and `reopen`
  (before the mutation applies).
- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` — call the helper in `comment`, `edit_ticket`, `link`
  (endpoint `id1`), `unlink` (endpoint `id1`), `tag`, `untag`, `archive`
  (before the mutation applies).
- `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` — call the helper in `set_file_impact` and
  `declare_no_file_impact` (before the mutation applies).
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` — document `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` and that single-ticket
  library functions emit it while bulk reads do not.

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit test** using the stdlib `warnings` capture (`pytest.warns` /
`warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)`) — the mechanism is entirely in-process
(test-design §3 pure/validation path). Real temporary tracker; acting session set via
`REBAR_SESSION_ID` (monkeypatch). Claim as holder A (`REBAR_SESSION_ID=A`, `rebar.claim`),
then set `REBAR_SESSION_ID=B` to act.

- With a ticket held by session A and acting session B, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits
  exactly one `CrossSessionWarning` whose message names holder `A`; assert the same for one
  write, e.g. `rebar.comment(<id>, "x")`, and confirm the write still applies.
- Negative control (same session): acting as A, assert **no** `CrossSessionWarning` is
  emitted (`catch_warnings(record=True)` list has none of that category).
- Bulk exclusion: `rebar.list_tickets()` / `rebar.ready()` as B emit no `CrossSessionWarning`.
- Unset-id silence: with `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits none.
- Category precision: the emitted warning is an instance of `rebar.CrossSessionWarning`
  (a `UserWarning` subclass), so a caller can filter it distinctly.
- Best-effort containment: when the detector raises (monkeypatch
  `cross_session_warning_for` to throw), the library call still returns normally and emits
  no `CrossSessionWarning`.
- Defect-seeded (mutation teeth): negate the `msg is not None` guard / point at the wrong
  endpoint and show the warn/silence assertions go RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` and `rebar.comment(<id>, ...)` each emit exactly one
  `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` naming holder `A` when acting as session B against an A-held
  ticket (checked by a `pytest.warns` test under `make test`).
- [ ] Negative control: acting as session A, no `CrossSessionWarning` is emitted by those
  functions (checked by `catch_warnings(record=True)` asserting none of that category).
- [ ] `rebar.list_tickets()` and `rebar.ready()` as session B emit no `CrossSessionWarning`
  for A's `in_progress` ticket (checked by a bulk-exclusion assertion).
- [ ] With `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits no `CrossSessionWarning`
  (checked by an unset-id assertion).
- [ ] The emitted warning is an instance of `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` subclassing
  `UserWarning` (checked by an `isinstance` assertion in the warns test).
- [ ] The emit is best-effort: when `cross_session_warning_for` raises, the single-ticket
  library call still returns normally and emits no `CrossSessionWarning` (checked by a test
  that monkeypatches the detector to raise and asserts the call's return is unchanged).
- [ ] `docs/reuse-surface.md` documents `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` and the single-ticket
  emission (checked: `grep -n "CrossSessionWarning" docs/reuse-surface.md` matches).
